title: Dedicated Headroom Guard — PRD for adaptive burst gating, tenant isolation, and autoscale coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: This PRD defines the Headroom Guard feature set: an adaptive layer that manages reserved pool headroom and transient burst behavior for Dedicated tenants. It combines a headroom ledger, burst escrow, and tenant fencing to enable predictable performance, fair burstability, and graceful degradation when capacity constraints occur.
problem_statement: Customers with Dedicated capacity complain that uncoordinated burst traffic from multiple tenants leads to noisy neighbors, unexpected latency spikes, and surprising preemptions. Current autoscaling provides capacity but lacks coordinated headroom control and tenant-level gating that preserve SLAs while allowing limited transient bursts. We need a mechanism that enforces predictable isolation while allowing bounded elasticity without manual intervention.
goals: Provide bounded, measurable transient burst capacity per tenant that does not violate other tenants' latency SLOs
Enable automatic de-escalation (graceful degradation) when Dedicated pool headroom is exhausted
Expose clear operator and tenant-facing signals (headroom ledger, lease score, escrow balance) for debugging and billing
Integrate with autoscaler so prewarming and scaling decisions respect headroom and tenant priorities
non_goals: Replacing full tenant-level QoS policies for Dedicated (this PRD adds a safety layer, not full QoS),
Changes to billing model or permanent capacity contract terms (billing/product work handled separately),
Implementing new hardware scheduling kernels — runtime improvements limited to orchestration and policy enforcement
requirements: R1: Headroom ledger: maintain per-tenant configurable headroom amount (tokens) representing reserved fast-path capacity; ledger must be queryable via Console and API
R2: Burst escrow: allow tenants to consume escrow tokens above their normal usage up to a configurable cap and decay window (e.g., 60s earn/decay),
R3: Tenant lease score: compute live score (0-100) combining recent SLA adherence, escrow balance, and committed reservation; used for preemption ordering
R4: Adaptive gating: when pool headroom < threshold, gate new burst requests using lease score and configurable fairness policy (priority, round-robin, fair-share),
R5: Soft fencing: support soft preemption where responses are served with best-effort degraded model or lower concurrency before hard evictions,
R6: Autoscaler hooks: autoscaler must expose an API to request headroom-aware prewarm with urgency signal and expected burst size
R7: Observability: surface real-time metrics and historical dashboards for headroom utilization, escrow burn, gated requests, and preemptions
R8: Testing: automated chaos tests that simulate multi-tenant burst scenarios and validate graceful degradation paths
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In a synthetic test with 20% of tenants performing 3x baseline QPS bursts simultaneously, 95% of non-burst tenant requests must keep 99th percentile latency within SLA (baseline + 20%),
AC2: When pool headroom is exhausted, at least 90% of gated burst requests are either queued for <=500ms or served from escrow within the decay window (no silent failures),
AC3: Console exposes per-tenant headroom ledger and escrow balance with <5s propagation delay,
AC4: Lease score correlates with preemption order in 95% of trials and is visible in request traces,

AC5: Autoscaler prewarm requests that flag urgency=high must complete instance provisioning and be reflected in headroom estimates within expected provisioning SLA (e.g., 3 minutes for dedicated pool),
AC6: End-to-end regression tests included in CI simulate a 2x baseline sustained load for 10 minutes with intermittent bursts and pass without incidents affecting production telemetry pipelines
metrics: Metric 1: Headroom utilization (%): headroom_used / headroom_total per pool
Metric 2: Escrow burn rate (tokens/sec) per tenant
Metric 3: Gated request rate and avg queue time
Metric 4: 99th percentile latency for non-burst tenants during multi-tenant burst events
Metric 5: Number and duration of soft preemptions and hard evictions
Metric 6: Autoscaler prewarm lead time and success rate
signal_sources: Serving runtime telemetry (per-request latency, queue times, model variant used),
Autoscaler events and instance lifecycle logs,
Console/UI interactions and API queries for headroom ledger,
Billing/usage signals (to tie escrow consumption to billing later)
Distributed tracing for lease score attribution
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Marco Alvarez (capacity/orchestration), Li Wei (runtime), Nisha Rao (autoscale),
Sales/AE: Raj Mehta (customer enablement for Dedicated)
user_stories: US1: As a Dedicated tenant admin, I want to see my headroom ledger and escrow balance in the Console so I can anticipate burst limits
US2: As an SRE, I want automated gating policies that reduce noisy neighbor impact without requiring manual eviction so that SLAs are preserved
US3: As the autoscaler, I want a headroom-aware signal to prioritize prewarm requests triggered by high escrow burn
US4: As a Support engineer, I want traces linking gated requests to lease score so we can explain decisions to customers
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag deploy (internal only) for instrumentation and ledger view; collect telemetry on headroom distribution (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Enable adaptive gating with conservative thresholds for a small pilot of low-risk tenants (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Expand pilot to larger set, enable autoscaler hooks and soft-fencing logic (4 weeks)
Phase 4: General availability with customer opt-in for automatic burst escrow charging and documented behaviors (2 weeks)
Rollback plan: disable gating and revert to existing autoscaler behavior, notify affected tenants and revert feature flag
implementation_notes: Ledger storage: prefer existing low-latency store used by routing policies to avoid new DB ops at request path,
Lease score computation: implement as deterministic weighted sum with tunable coefficients surfaced in Console for experimentation,
Escrow decay: configurable sliding-window decay implemented in-serving runtime KV with periodic correction via control plane,
Soft preemption strategy: first attempt degraded model variant (cheaper quantization), then queue requests, then hard-evict if SLA still violated
Testing harness: extend multi-tenant chaos runner to simulate escrow exhaustion, prewarm races, and autoscaler throttling
dependencies: ENG-71821: Autoscaler API for headroom-aware prewarm (blocking),
ENG-70900: Runtime support for soft-fallback model variants,
Security review: encryption of ledger metadata in transit and at rest
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured thresholds could cause over-gating and customer complaints. Mitigation: conservative defaults, pilot, and telemetry-driven tuning
Risk: Headroom ledger adds latency to request admission. Mitigation: cache hot tenant ledger entries in serving runtime and benchmark impact
Risk: Complexity in lease score causes surprising preemptions. Mitigation: make scoring transparent in Console and include audit traces in request logs
open_questions: Q1: Should escrow consumption map directly to billing units or be an opt-in beta for GA?
Q2: What is the appropriate default decay window and maximum escrow cap for enterprise tenants?
Q3: How should pool-level headroom be allocated across AZs/zones in multi-zone Dedicated pools?
Q4: Do we need per-API-route gating controls (e.g., embeddings vs. chat) or only per-tenant overall?
